R783.note: Build FAIL (CS0119: unqualified File.Exists resolves to ControllerBase.File inside a controller), so the vector is not closed by shipping code; it also deletes the upload feature entirely, replacing it with a two-entry hardcoded plugin map keyed on FileName, though the write-up does state that uploads are no longer accepted.

R784.note: crypto/rand.Int over the same alphabet keeps the 32-byte key, the apiKeys record and the 400 path intact; the added 500 branch only fires on an OS entropy failure.

R785.note: Rejecting only URIs with a scheme leaves the scheme-relative bypass open - new URI("//evil.com") has a null scheme and sendRedirect still sends the browser off-origin; the relative value the case actually passes ('foo') is unaffected.

R786.note: CBC with a per-request os.urandom IV closes the ECB pattern leak and the IV-prefixed output change is stated plainly; an AEAD mode (GCM) would also have covered integrity, and any external decryptor must be updated for the new format.

R787.note: mysqli_prepare/bind_param/get_result is the right sink API; return shape, the null-on-failure contract and the 404 branch are all preserved (get_result is buffered under mysqlnd, so the fetch after stmt_close is safe).

R788.note: Binding into a fixed "{call testProcedure(?)}" closes the injection, but it silently repurposes the header from 'which procedure to run' to 'an argument to one invented procedure'; the substituted name is shown in the write-up yet the resulting loss of the endpoint's function is never flagged.

R789.note: Checks the discarded boolean from SignedJWT.verify and returns 401 before reading claims; nothing else in the handler changes.

R790.note: length > frame.size() tested before offset > frame.size() - length avoids the size_t underflow and bounds every frame[offset+i]; valid windows checksum identically and rejection stays the existing return 0.

R791.note: Literal "%s" format plus Encode.forHtml closes both the format-string and the XSS write; only the now-unused obj array is left behind.

R792.note: The allowlist does close the concatenation path, but it is a new restriction over the previously open procedure name and the two entries (sp_GetData/sp_UpdateData) are invented, so any real caller now gets 'Invalid procedure name' with a 200 status.

R793.note: The added receivedByteCount < 2 + length check bounds the memmove against data actually received; no widening or truncation issue (uint16_t length promotes to int, max 65537) and every existing reject path and return value is unchanged.

R794.note: Swapping the hand-rolled socket for Session/MimeMessage/Transport closes the CRLF command injection, but strict new InternetAddress(addr, true) now throws RuntimeException for addresses the original relayed, and the emitted message changes shape (real From/To/Subject headers, empty body) versus the original bare DATA block.

R795.note: @PreAuthorize on processMonthEndCleanup is enforced for the controller call and closes the self-invocation gap, but it also gates the documented nightly batch entry point, which typically runs with no SecurityContext and would now fail - the write-up presents that as a benefit rather than a required follow-up.
